topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the framework for cancer evolution, and presents the key learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Clonal Selection and Epigenetic Dynamics in Cancer Development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how pre-malignant growths evolve toward malignancy through the Darwinian selection of advantageous mutations alongside non-mutational epigenetic alterations.

topics.label: Stem Cell Hierarchies and Cell of Origin in Tumorigenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine whether cancers initiate within tissue-specific stem cells or differentiated progenitor cells through hierarchical and stochastic models.

topics.label: Microenvironmental and Inflammatory Influences on Tumor Progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics demonstrate how inflammatory signals, environmental promoting factors, and supportive stromal cells cooperate to enable both incipient and established tumor outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Studying Cancer Evolution and the Microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews the genomic, spatial, and computational technologies employed in the laboratory to map tumor evolution and microenvironmental interactions.

topics.label: Multi-Factor Evolutionary Framework of Cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic synthesizes how the convergence of mutational burden, cell of origin, epigenetic plasticity, and microenvironmental conditions drives cancer evolution.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer ends the lecture and previews the next session on cancer therapy.
